description:
Enterprise dual-homed BGP scenario with redundant ISP connections. Configure eBGP peering with two ISPs (AS 65001 and AS 65002), implement outbound and inbound route filtering using prefix-lists and route-maps, configure local-preference for primary/backup path selection, and implement AS-PATH prepending for inbound traffic engineering. Verify failover behavior and optimize convergence times. Based on CCIE Service Provider and Enterprise lab scenarios.

IP Addressing Plan:
- EDGE1: eth1=203.0.113.2/30 (to ISP1), eth2=10.0.1.1/30 (to CORE), lo=10.0.0.1/32
- EDGE2: eth1=198.51.100.2/30 (to ISP2), eth2=10.0.2.1/30 (to CORE), lo=10.0.0.2/32
- ISP1: eth1=203.0.113.1/30, lo=1.1.1.1/32
- ISP2: eth1=198.51.100.1/30, lo=2.2.2.2/32
- CORE: eth1=10.0.1.2/30, eth2=10.0.2.2/30, lo=10.0.0.100/32

properties.description: eBGP session with ISP1 (AS 65001) is established
eBGP session with ISP2 (AS 65002) is established
Outbound route filtering: only enterprise prefixes advertised to ISPs
Local preference configured for primary path selection (ISP1 preferred)
AS-PATH prepending on backup path for inbound traffic engineering
BGP convergence optimization: timers tuned for faster failover (<60s)

evaluation.command: vtysh -c 'show ip bgp neighbors' | grep 'Hold time'

optimal_solution.description: Configure BGP ASN, establish eBGP peers with both ISPs, create prefix-lists for filtering, configure route-maps for local-pref and AS-PATH manipulation, tune BGP timers (keepalive 10s, holdtime 30s), verify peering and routing policy

research_context.citation: CCIE Service Provider and Enterprise lab exam format (8+ hours total, this represents 1 major scenario). BGP convergence optimization research: default BGP hold time 180s can be reduced to 30s with BFD for sub-second detection (Noction BGP optimization whitepaper). Complex BGP deployments: hours to days for policy manipulation and traffic engineering (Catchpoint BGP analysis).
research_context.literature_basis: Dual-homed BGP is a standard enterprise/SP scenario covered in CCIE R&S and SP labs. Design based on RFC 4271 (BGP-4), Cisco CCIE official cert guide, and common ISP multi-homing best practices. AS-PATH prepending and local-preference manipulation are standard BGP policy techniques documented in IETF RFCs and vendor best practice guides.
research_context.time_justification: 120 minutes (2 hours) represents realistic time for expert-level BGP configuration with policy optimization. CCIE candidates spend 12-24 months preparing, with individual lab scenarios taking 1-3 hours. This task is scoped as one complete BGP scenario within a larger CCIE-style lab.
